effect: The final result explains that placing the mark inside the focal distance produces an upright, enlarged virtual image, distinct from the screen projection.
reaction: The contrast between a viewed virtual image and a projected image made the lens result more interesting.

mostWorthwhile.text: Combining the lens with the light-path account was most worthwhile: it connected placement to magnification and distinguished a virtual image from a projection.

leastWorthwhile.text: Shaping the glass blank was the least engaging passage; it produced a lens but gave little detail about how the shaping worked.

surprise.text: The explanation that outgoing rays diverge yet appear to come from a larger virtual image changed my understanding of the close-up view.

arbitrary.text: No action felt clearly purposeless, though the lens-making combination was offered as compatible rather than something I had to work out.

continue.text: I would continue into another chapter: the comparison of projection and magnification made me curious about other applications of light paths, although the largely forced choices were less compelling.
